title: The Best 7-Passenger SUVs of 2026
summary: There are lots of 7-seater SUVs out there, but which are the best? Our expert guide has the lowdown, with full details of the 3-row SUVs you should be considering above all others.
body_markdown:
When the time comes to transport more than a handful of people, a 7-passenger SUV is often the perfect solution. These vehicles offer the versatility to handle everything from the daily school run to a cross-country family road trip, blending the passenger capacity of a minivan with the rugged styling and available all-wheel-drive capability of an SUV. With three rows of seating, they provide the flexibility to carry a full load of passengers or fold down the rear seats to create a cavernous cargo area for luggage, sports equipment, or home improvement supplies.


The modern 7-passenger SUV market is more diverse than ever, offering a wide range of options to suit nearly any need or budget. Shoppers can choose from efficient hybrids and fully electric models like the Hyundai Ioniq 9, luxurious and powerful options such as the BMW X7 and Lincoln Aviator, or practical and value-packed choices like the Kia Telluride and Honda Pilot. Whether you prioritize a premium interior, engaging driving dynamics, cutting-edge technology, or maximum cargo space, there's a three-row SUV designed to meet your family's demands.


Our recommendations are based on a comprehensive evaluation that combines the expert opinions of our seasoned test drivers, real-world feedback from vehicle owners, and in-depth market analysis. We consider everything from performance and practicality to overall value. The Overall CarGurus rating for each vehicle is determined by a proprietary algorithm that factors in our expert ratings, user reviews, and the percentage of "Good" or "Great" deals available on CarGurus, giving you a complete picture of what makes a car a smart buy.

The 2026 Hyundai Palisade continues to set the bar high among three-row SUVs, thanks to its comprehensive redesign focused on family comfort and real-world usability. The Palisade's cabin is both refined and roomy, offering configurations for seven or eight passengers. Hyundai’s thoughtful approach extends to cargo space as well, with up to 20.2 cubic feet behind the third row and a generous 86.7 cubic feet with the rear seats folded—plenty for family road trips or big grocery runs. The new Palisade also boasts a more upright, squared-off exterior and a softer, mid-century modern-inspired interior, making it a top pick for shoppers who want style and substance in their next family vehicle.


Under the hood, the Palisade is powered by a 3.5-liter V6 producing 287 hp and 260 lb-ft of torque, delivering smooth and refined performance that’s well suited for daily driving and highway cruising alike. Tech features are generous across the lineup, including a 12.3-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, advanced safety tech, and available luxury touches like heated and ventilated seats all the way to the third row. Add in Hyundai’s impressive warranty coverage and a strong mix of good and great deals on CarGurus, and the 2026 Palisade stands out as a smart, family-friendly choice among the best 7-passenger SUVs of 2026.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"The 2026 Hyundai Palisade is an improvement over the outgoing version it replaces in every meaningful way. Consider the Palisade a top choice if you’re in the market for a three-row SUV that’s comfortable for the whole family." - Jeremy Korzeniewski*

## 2. Lincoln Aviator


**CarGurus expert rating:** 7.7 out of 10

For shoppers who want a three-row SUV with a premium feel, the 2026 Lincoln Aviator leans into the comfort side of the 7-passenger equation. Its smooth ride and cosseting cabin make it an easy vehicle to live with on commutes and longer road trips, especially for families who want a quieter, more relaxed experience than you’ll typically get in a mainstream three-row SUV.


The trade-off is that the Aviator’s luxury is paired with some real-world compromises for a family hauler, including an awkward feel when driven hard and a third row that isn’t as comfortable as you’d hope for frequent adult use. It also asks you to pay a premium despite its close relationship to the Ford Explorer underneath, though it still brings practical strengths like a decent towing capacity for things like a small camper or boat.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"The 2026 Lincoln Aviator expands on the strengths of the Ford Explorer on which it’s based, while also introducing some compromises." - Kirk Bell*

## 3. Kia Telluride


**CarGurus expert rating:** 8.2 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.7 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 32.9%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.6 out of 5


Pros Cons

Comfortable Irritating lane-assist system


Great safety ratings Sticky brakes in thick traffic


The Kia Telluride offers families a blend of comfort, versatility, and style. Every Telluride is powered by a smooth 3.8-liter V6 engine producing 291 hp and 262 lb-ft of torque, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission. On the road, the Telluride impresses with its refined ride and available all-wheel drive, while thoughtful touches like heated and ventilated first- and second-row seats, ample charging options, and clever storage solutions make it a favorite for long family trips. Behind the third row, you’ll find 21 cubic feet of cargo space—enough for most family needs—but folding the seats expands capacity to 87 cubic feet, making it easy to haul luggage, sports gear, or home improvement supplies.


Kia hasn’t rested on its laurels: even as some rivals switch to turbocharged four-cylinders, the Telluride’s V6 remains a highlight for those who value traditional smoothness and ample power. Safety is another major strength. The Telluride boasts a five-star NHTSA crash rating and Top Safety Pick+ honors from the IIHS. Standard advanced driver aids, including Highway Driving Assist, adaptive cruise control, and a surround-view camera, deliver extra peace of mind. While the infotainment tech is due for an update and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto require a wired connection, the Telluride’s robust value, upscale design, and strong owner satisfaction keep it at the top of the class for 7-passenger SUVs.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"Aging technology caused some irritation during a five-day road trip in the 2025 Kia Telluride. Otherwise, the Telluride was perfectly suited to long-distance travel–whether rolling down an Interstate, roaming a major city, or romping down trails near a national park." - Christian Wardlaw*

## 4. Volvo XC90


**CarGurus expert rating:** 8.3 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.7 out of 5

**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.6 out of 5

The Volvo XC90 continues to set the bar for midsize three-row luxury SUVs, making it a top pick for families seeking both style and versatility in a 7-passenger vehicle. With its latest refresh, the XC90 keeps its timeless Scandinavian design while updating features and materials to meet modern expectations. The interior is airy and comfortable across all three rows, and Volvo’s clever reorganization of the center console and standard wireless charging pad make everyday usability and small-item storage much more convenient. Whether you’re loading up the family or need flexible cargo space, the XC90’s layout and thoughtful amenities ensure a smooth experience for drivers and passengers alike.


Performance is another standout, with three powertrains to choose from, all featuring standard all-wheel drive. The base B5 mild-hybrid four-cylinder offers 247 hp and 266 lb-ft of torque, while the B6 bumps up to 295 hp and 310 lb-ft of torque for more spirited driving. For those focused on efficiency, the T8 plug-in hybrid delivers an impressive 455 hp and 523 lb-ft of torque, along with up to 33 miles of pure electric driving—ideal for short commutes or errands. Safety remains a core strength, as Volvo’s reputation is reinforced by top crash-test ratings for previous model years and a suite of advanced driver-assistance systems that work seamlessly in real-world conditions.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"With a starting price just under $60,000 and a host of luxury touches, the XC90 offers strong value and a “stealth wealth” appeal that stands out among the best SUVs for families." - Natalie Harrington*

## 5. BMW X7


**CarGurus expert rating:** 7.3 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.8 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 35.3%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.5 out of 5


Pros Cons


Great handling Potentially polarizing design


Easy-to-use technology Unimpressive interior materials


Reasonable value for money


BMW’s largest SUV, the X7, is designed for families who want to travel in style and comfort without sacrificing engaging driving dynamics. Offering both six- and seven-passenger configurations, the X7 stands out in its class for its competitive headroom across all three rows and its versatile cargo space—delivering up to 48.6 cubic feet behind the second row and 90.4 cubic feet with both rear rows folded. The base xDrive40i comes with a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six engine producing 375 hp and 398 lb-ft of torque, while the M60i xDrive raises the stakes with a 523-hp twin-turbo V8. For those seeking ultimate performance, the Alpina XB7 boasts a thrilling 631 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque, sprinting from 0-60 mph in just 3.9 seconds.


Inside, the X7 blends high-tech features with practical touches. The BMW Curved Display houses a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a 14.9-inch touchscreen, supported by the user-friendly iDrive 8.5 infotainment system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Standard driver assists include forward collision warning, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keep assist, while advanced features like hands-free Highway Assistant are optional. Despite some mixed interior material quality, the X7 offers strong value—starting at $87,875, it undercuts several rivals in the luxury SUV market while delivering a balanced mix of sportiness, utility, and family-friendly space.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"BMW loyalists will find more of what they love about the brand, while the X7’s superb driving dynamics and reasonable pricing (for this high-end segment, that is) should give customers of rival brands something to think about." - Stephen Edelstein*

## 6. Honda Pilot


**CarGurus expert rating:** 7 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.7 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 30.7%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.5 out of 5


Pros Cons


Practical for daily living Unimpressive fuel economy


Plenty of cargo space Technology looks outdated


Great safety ratings Front passenger seat lacks adjustment


Few three-row SUVs have cracked the passenger space puzzle quite like the 2026 Honda Pilot. Its standout feature is the removable second-row center seat — giving owners the flexibility to switch between bench and captain's chair configurations without sacrificing either option permanently. The seat stows neatly under the cargo floor in a dedicated compartment, and the outboard second-row seats are genuinely spacious for adults, sliding fore and aft by a generous amount and reclining for longer trips. Third-row access is as easy as a single button push, which folds and slides the second row forward automatically. With up to 112.4 cubic feet of cargo space when both rows are folded, the Pilot's versatility rivals a minivan. Powering it all is a 285-horsepower 3.5-liter V6 paired with a 10-speed automatic, with AWD standard on most trims.


The Pilot's appeal on this list goes beyond raw seating numbers, though — it's the thoughtful details that set it apart from less imaginative rivals. A Cabin Talk feature uses the audio system as an intercom so the driver can communicate with rear-row passengers without raising their voice, and multiple camera angles assist with tight parking and light off-roading. For 2026, Honda upgrades to a standard 12.3-inch touchscreen and a 10.2-inch digital instrument panel across all trims, with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto included. The Honda Sensing suite of safety features — adaptive cruise control, lane-keep assist, blind-spot monitoring, and automatic emergency braking among them — comes standard on every Pilot. The 2025 model earned a five-star NHTSA overall rating and IIHS Top Safety Pick recognition, and with no structural changes for 2026, similarly strong results are expected.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"Clever features help the Pilot stand out from other three-row SUVs. Our only major complaint is the lack of a more fuel-efficient model." - Mark Takahashi*

## 7. Mitsubishi Outlander


**CarGurus expert rating:** 6.7 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.5 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 33.8%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.5 out of 5


Pros Cons


Impressive stereo Potentially polarizing design


Comfortable Cramped third row


Quiet cabin Sluggish performance


If you occasionally need three rows but would rather not have a larger vehicle, the Mitsubishi Outlander is one of few compact crossovers with standard third-row seating. While the rearmost seats offer a tight 18.7 inches of legroom, the Outlander shines in cargo flexibility, providing nearly 30 cubic feet of storage space with the third row folded. For families seeking comfort and convenience, the Outlander’s interior brings welcome improvements for 2025, with available quilted leather seats, soft-touch surfaces, and easy-to-use physical controls for climate and infotainment. The new Yamaha sound system is a highlight, delivering premium audio with up to 12 speakers and advanced settings tailored for every passenger.


On the road, the Outlander’s 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine produces 181 hp and 181 lb-ft of torque—adequate for daily driving but less spirited than some rivals. The ride benefits from updated suspension tuning for a more composed feel, though acceleration is best described as modest. Tech features include a crisp 12.3-inch infotainment screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, USB-C ports, and a wireless charging pad. Safety is solid, with essential driver aids standard and additional features available on higher trims. Mitsubishi’s generous warranty—10 years/100,000 miles for the powertrain—adds peace of mind, and the Outlander’s competitive starting price makes it a sensible pick for budget-minded families needing occasional seven-passenger capability.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"The Mitsubishi Outlander still isn’t the best-driving crossover you can buy, and the front fascia might turn you off, but the small improvements and excellent sound system might inspire some buyers to visit the dealership." - Emme Hall*

## 8. Volkswagen Atlas


**CarGurus expert rating:** 6.8 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.7 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 34.6%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.5 out of 5


Pros Cons


Stylish design Poor ride quality


High-end interior Unintuitive technology


Plenty of cargo space Pedestrian performance


Few three-row SUVs make as strong a first impression as the Volkswagen Atlas, and fewer still back it up with genuinely competitive passenger and cargo space. The cabin is one of the segment's most upscale at this price point, with quilted diamond-pattern leather, metallic accents, and warm wood trim in upper trims that put it in the same visual league as vehicles costing significantly more. All three rows are thoughtfully executed: the front seats offer heat, ventilation, and massage on the top trim, the second-row captain's chairs fold and tip forward without collapsing (a godsend when a car seat is installed), and the third-row bench sits high enough off the floor to provide real thigh support—something many competitors miss. Cargo capacity is a genuine competitive advantage, with 20.6 cubic feet behind the third row, 55.5 cubic feet with it folded, and a class-competitive 96.6 cubic feet total. A five-star NHTSA overall safety rating and a standard IQ.Drive suite—bundling adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keep assist, and semi-autonomous Travel Assist across every trim—round out a strong value proposition, with base pricing starting below most rivals in the segment.


On the road, the turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder delivers 269 hp and 273 lb-ft of torque with a wide, usable powerband that keeps highway driving relaxed and composed. AWD is available across the lineup and standard on the Peak Edition and above, with a dedicated Snow mode for added confidence in slippery conditions. The main trade-offs are well-documented: ride quality on larger wheel-and-tire packages can feel stiff and harsh over rough pavement, and the native MIB3 infotainment system is genuinely frustrating to use. The good news on both counts is that smaller wheels on lower trims may smooth things out, and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto work flawlessly as a daily alternative to the native system. For families who want a seven-passenger SUV that looks premium, hauls people and cargo with ease, and undercuts much of the competition on price, the Atlas makes a compelling case.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *" The 2026 Volkswagen Atlas delivers on its core promise of style and space at a non-luxury price point. If you can tolerate its subpar ride quality and maddening infotainment system—or if you simply plan to rely on Apple CarPlay and ignore the native tech—this handsome three-row SUV offers compelling value for shoppers prioritizing looks and space."* - Matt Smith, CarGurus Head of Content

## 9. Mazda CX-90


**CarGurus expert rating:** 6.2 out of 10
**CarGurus user rating:** 4.5 out of 5
**Percentage of Good and Great Deals available on CarGurus:** 34.0%
**Overall CarGurus rating:** 4.4 out of 5


Pros Cons


Stylish design Underwhelming base engine


Premium interior materials Noisy


Great safety ratings Unintuitive technology


The Mazda CX-90 offers elegant design and premium interior touches that rival luxury brands, but at a more accessible price point. Available with a turbocharged 3.3-liter inline-six engine (280 hp and 332 lb-ft of torque) or as a plug-in hybrid, the CX-90 delivers a driving experience that's both engaging and refined. Inside, you'll find Nappa leather, polished metallic trim, and seating for up to seven passengers, though third-row space is best suited for children. Cargo space behind the third row measures 14.9 cubic feet, expanding to 40 cubic feet with the rear seats folded, which is practical but not class-leading.


Where the CX-90 truly shines is in safety, earning a Top Safety Pick+ from the IIHS and five-star NHTSA ratings for its PHEV variant. Standard safety features include adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking, and blind-spot monitoring, with more advanced driver aids available on higher trims. On the tech front, Mazda's infotainment system still relies mostly on a rotary controller rather than a touchscreen, which takes some getting used to. Despite its stylish look and solid ride, some drivers may find the base engine and certain tech controls less intuitive than competitors.


**The CarGurus Verdict:** *"With more attention to detail and better technology, this Mazda SUV could lead instead of follow." - Christian Wardlaw*

With seating for seven, an impressive estimated range of up to 335 miles (S trim), and a federal EV tax credit that makes it more accessible, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 stands out as a practical choice for families shopping for a three-row electric SUV. The Ioniq 9’s spacious interior benefits from Hyundai’s dedicated EV architecture, featuring flat floors for easy movement and 21.9 cubic feet of cargo space behind the third row—expanding to 86.9 cubic feet with all rear seats folded. Access is a breeze thanks to wide-opening rear doors, and the available captain’s chairs (on Limited and Calligraphy trims) offer comfort for longer drives.


Under the hood, the Ioniq 9 offers a range of powertrains: the base S trim uses a single 215-hp rear motor, while all other trims upgrade to dual-motor all-wheel drive, with the Limited and Calligraphy trims delivering up to 422 hp. While the Ioniq 9 isn’t tuned for sporty handling—its soft suspension prioritizes comfort over cornering—it impresses with a quiet, pillowy ride and excellent energy efficiency (up to 3.2 miles per kWh observed). Tech features abound, including standard dual 12.3-inch displays, wireless smartphone integration, a robust set of advanced safety features, and up to six USB-C ports to keep the whole family charged and connected.
